name: Clickjacking (Frame-Based UI Redress)
description: UI-redress attack that frames a target application inside an invisible/transparent iframe over decoy content, so the victim's clicks land on sensitive controls (delete account, change email, approve OAuth, transfer funds) they cannot see. Exploits missing X-Frame-Options / CSP frame-ancestors. Covers the opacity-overlay PoC, drag-and-drop and prefilled-form variants, and chaining a framed action with a prefilled input.
notes:
=== WHY IT WORKS === If a page can be framed (no X-Frame-Options / no CSP frame-ancestors), an attacker overlays it transparently on top of bait content and aligns a decoy button under a real sensitive control. The victim 'clicks the bait' but actually clicks the framed app while authenticated. === BASIC OPACITY-OVERLAY PoC ===
Align the decoy button under the real 'Confirm' button (tweak top/left; set opacity to 0.5 while aligning, then to ~0). === PREFILLED-FORM VARIANT === - Load the framed app with a URL that prefills a form (e.g. /email/change?email=attacker@evil.com) so a single framed click submits attacker data. === DRAG-AND-DROP / MULTISTEP === - Trick the user into dragging a token into a field, or chain two aligned clicks. === BYPASS NOTES === - frame-busting JS alone is weak; test if the site relies only on JS (sandbox the iframe to neuter busting:

examples.label: Prefilled form so one click submits attacker data

recommended.note: Both coerce victim interaction - phishing form vs invisible frame.
Another client-side trust-boundary flaw to test on the same app.
framed pages often also expose postMessage origin flaws.

defense.why_it_works: Without X-Frame-Options or a CSP frame-ancestors directive, the browser lets any site embed the app in an iframe. An attacker renders it transparently over decoy content so authenticated clicks are redirected to sensitive controls.
defense.prerequisites: A sensitive, state-changing page that can be framed (no anti-framing header) and a victim who is authenticated and interacts with the attacker's bait page.
defense.impact: Unintended sensitive actions performed as the victim - account deletion, email/password change, OAuth consent, fund transfer, or privilege changes - without stealing credentials.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1185] Largely a client-side attack with limited server telemetry; look for sensitive-action requests whose Referer/Sec-Fetch-Dest indicate an iframe/cross-site origin, and for responses that are being served without framing-protection headers.
defense.artifacts: Web access logs with Referer and Sec-Fetch-Dest=iframe / Sec-Fetch-Site=cross-site on sensitive endpoints, and header-audit reports showing missing X-Frame-Options / frame-ancestors.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=web (uri_path="/account/delete" OR uri_path="/email/change")
| rex field=_raw "Sec-Fetch-Dest:\s*(?<dest>\S+)"
| rex field=_raw "Sec-Fetch-Site:\s*(?<site>\S+)"
| where dest="iframe" OR site="cross-site"
| stats count by clientip, uri_path, site
defense.sentinel_kql:
W3CIISLog
| where csUriStem in ("/account/delete","/email/change")
| extend secFetchSite = extract(@"Sec-Fetch-Site:\s*(\S+)", 1, csHeaders)
| where secFetchSite == "cross-site"
| summarize count() by cIP, csUriStem
defense.prevention: Send Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'self' (or an explicit allow-list) on all pages, plus X-Frame-Options: DENY/SAMEORIGIN for legacy browsers. Require re-authentication or an un-prefillable confirmation step for destructive actions. Set SameSite cookies. Do not rely on JavaScript frame-busting alone.

detections.name: Sensitive action requested from a cross-site iframe context
detections.logic:
index=web sourcetype=nginx (uri_path="/account/delete" OR uri_path="/email/change")
| rex field=_raw "Sec-Fetch-Dest:\s*(?<dest>\S+)"
| rex field=_raw "Sec-Fetch-Site:\s*(?<site>\S+)"
| where dest="iframe" OR site="cross-site"
| stats count by clientip, uri_path, site
detections.false_positives: Legitimate embedded widgets or same-org iframes; older browsers omit Sec-Fetch-* headers.
detections.tuning: Combine with the absence of framing-protection headers on the response and focus on destructive endpoints only.
